input.quote: 8.1 By Commerce One. Commerce One shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Corio and its Customers from any and all damages, liabilities, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees) incurred by Corio or its Customers arising out of any claim that the Software infringes any patent, copyright, trademark or trade right secret of a third party
input.rationale: Section 8.1 gives us (and our Customers) a full defend-and-indemnify from Commerce One for third-party claims that the Software infringes patent, copyright, trademark or trade secret rights, with standard procedure (prompt notice, tender of control to the vendor at its expense, cooperation at its expense, right to join with our own counsel) and the standard remedy ladder of procure / modify or replace / terminate and refund a pro-rated portion of fees. Exclusions in 8.2 are the usual narrow ones (use outside the Documentation; third-party modification where the infringement would not otherwise have occurred) and do not include combination or Corio-specification carve-outs. Critically, Section 9 carves liability "ARISING UNDER SECTION 8" out of both the 12-month fee cap and the consequential-damages exclusion, so the vendor indemnity is uncapped — better than the fallback's 3x annual fees super-cap. There is no reciprocal Corio indemnity anywhere (Section 6 trademark provisions impose approval/compliance obligations but no hold-harmless), so no one-way or over-broad customer indemnity to narrow. The clause therefore sits at or above the fallback and is not redlined. Noted only for the file, not as deviations: the indemnity does not extend to Commerce One's breach of applicable law, unauthorised access to or disclosure of Corio data, or its gross negligence/wilful misconduct, and it is limited to the Software rather than covering affiliates expressly — points we could raise if the section is reopened for other reasons.
